title: Branding and Trademark Checklist for Local Product Manufacturers
metaTitle: Branding & Trademark Checklist for Manufacturers | BRNDNUR
metaDescription: Essential pre-launch intellectual property and brand protection checklist for small-scale and industrial product manufacturers across Kerala.
primaryKeyword: branding and trademark checklist for local product manufacturers
intendedAudience: Small-scale factory owners, light engineering workshops, construction material makers, plastic molders, and consumer goods manufacturers across Kerala.
quickAnswer: Local product manufacturers in Kerala must protect their commercial brand identity through a structured five-step intellectual property checklist: 1) Conduct an exhaustive clearance search on the IP India database, 2) Choose an arbitrary or coined brand name, 3) Select primary and allied Nice classes, 4) Secure an Udyam MSME certificate to claim a 50% government fee discount (₹4,500 per class on Form TM-A), and 5) File both wordmark and packaging trade dress applications before commercial distribution.

h2Sections.h2: The Vulnerability of Product Manufacturers in Competitive Markets
content: Across Kerala's industrial corridors—from Kanjikode in Palakkad and Kalamassery in Ernakulam to Mattannur in Kannur and Kanhangad in Kasaragod—small and medium manufacturing enterprises (SMEs) produce exceptional products: modular furniture, electrical switches, plastic packaging, construction blocks, agricultural tools, and consumer goods.

However, many factory owners focus exclusively on plant machinery, raw material procurement, and wholesale distribution, treating branding and trademark registration as an afterthought. This creates severe commercial vulnerability. When an unbranded or unregistered product gains market traction, unscrupulous competitors or rogue distributors frequently register the brand name themselves, cutting off the original manufacturer from their own market.

h2Sections.h2: Phase 1: Brand Conception and Trademark Clearance
content: Before cutting dies, fabricating molds, or printing thousands of product cartons, manufacturers must validate brand name availability:
1. Avoid Purely Descriptive Names: Names that describe what the product does (e.g., 'Strong Blocks' or 'Sharp Tools') cannot be registered under Section 9(1)(b) of the Trade Marks Act.
2. Avoid Geographic Monopolies: Names including town or district names (e.g., 'Kasaragod Pipes' or 'Malabar Cement') will be rejected by examiners.
3. Adopt Coined or Arbitrary Words: Invent new words (e.g., 'DuraVelo' or 'TorqMax'). Coined words pass examination smoothly and provide ironclad legal protection.
4. IP India Public Database Search: Query the public trademark registry across all relevant goods classes using exact, phonetic, and wildcard search parameters.
The following matrix outlines the foundational steps every manufacturing enterprise must execute to secure its intellectual property:

Query wordmark, phonetic, and Vienna codes on IP India portal

Eliminates risk of infringing existing registered marks

h2Sections.h2: Phase 3: Classification Mapping Across Product and Service Lines
content: Manufacturers must avoid filing in only one narrow class. A complete legal shield requires multi-class architecture:

Primary Product Class: Cover the physical manufactured item (e.g., Class 6 for metal hardware, Class 19 for building materials, Class 20 for furniture, Class 17 for rubber/plastics, Class 7 for machines).

Allied Retail & Showroom Services (Class 35): Cover 'wholesale distribution, retail store services, dealership networks, and online sales.' This prevents unauthorized trading entities from opening showrooms bearing your exact brand moniker.
Custom Fabrication Services (Class 40): If offering custom contract manufacturing or OEM fabrication for third-party clients, file under Class 40.
checklist: Clear phonetic search report across primary manufacturing classes
Udyam MSME certificate linked to PAN to claim 50% government fee concession
High-resolution vector files of the logo and packaging carton layout
Notarized user affidavit with historical tax invoices if claiming prior use
Signed Form TM-48 power of attorney authorizing trademark representation

h2Sections.h2: Enforcement: Protecting Factory Output from Counterfeiting
content: Holding registered trademarks across your product lines gives you immediate statutory power to halt imitation:

1. Ex-Parte Search and Seizure (Anton Piller Orders): Under Section 135 of the Trade Marks Act, obtain civil court orders empowering court commissioners to raid competitor warehouses and seize counterfeit goods.
2. Criminal Action (Section 115): File police complaints resulting in the raid and confiscation of fake manufacturing dies, packaging cartons, and imitation goods.
3. Digital Marketplace Takedowns: Remove unauthorized third-party resellers attempting to pass off generic items as your branded industrial products on Indiamart, TradeIndia, and Amazon.

callout.title: Never Print Packaging Before Filing
callout.text: Never invest in printing bulk cartons or fabricating metal dies before obtaining your trademark application number on Form TM-A. If a conflict emerges later, discarding pre-printed inventory creates severe financial losses.

faqs.question: Can I trademark the shape of a manufactured product or container?
faqs.answer: Yes. Under Indian trademark law, three-dimensional shape marks (3D marks) can be registered if the shape is distinctive and not purely functional or dictated by the technical nature of the product.

faqs.question: What is the official government fee for a manufacturing company filing a trademark?
faqs.answer: For an enterprise holding a valid Udyam MSME certificate (or an individual proprietor), the official government fee on Form TM-A is ₹4,500 per class. For standard non-MSME corporate bodies, the official fee is ₹9,000 per class.

faqs.question: Can an OEM manufacturer register a trademark for goods made for other brands?
faqs.answer: An OEM manufacturer can register its own proprietary brand for its house products. However, they cannot register trademarks belonging to third-party clients for whom they provide contract manufacturing.
